income_tax_structure: Income tax rates should rise much more steeply with income, with a top rate above 50% on the highest earners.
The highest earners should pay higher rates than today, while middle incomes pay the same or less.
Keep today's seven rates, from 10% to 37%.
There should be only two or three income tax rates, with the top one at 30% or less.
Everyone should pay one flat rate on income above a basic tax-free amount.
There should be no federal income tax; the money should come from something else, such as a national sales tax.
low_income_tax: Low-income households should owe no federal income tax and get bigger refundable credits than they do today.
Low-income households should owe no federal income tax and keep about today's refundable credits.
Low-income households should owe no federal income tax, but their refundable credits should be smaller than today.
Every household, including low-income ones, should pay at least a small income tax, such as $100 a year.
Low-income households should pay the same flat rate as everyone else, starting from their first dollar.
tax_burden_principle: People with high incomes should pay a much bigger share of their income in taxes than people with low incomes.
People with high incomes should pay a somewhat bigger share of their income in taxes.
Everyone should pay the same share of their income, after a basic amount that isn't taxed.
Everyone should pay the same share of all their income, with no amount left untaxed.
top_income_tax: Income taxes on people earning over $1 million a year should go up a lot.
Income taxes on people earning over $1 million a year should go up somewhat.
Income taxes on people earning over $1 million a year should stay about where they are.
Income taxes on people earning over $1 million a year should come down somewhat.
Income taxes on people earning over $1 million a year should come down a lot.
top_rate_number: Each dollar earned above $1 million should be taxed at 70% or more.

Each dollar earned above $1 million should be taxed at about 40% to 45%.
Each dollar earned above $1 million should be taxed at 37%, as it is today.
Each dollar earned above $1 million should be taxed at about 25% to 30%.
Each dollar earned above $1 million should be taxed at 20% or less.
corporate_rate: Corporate profits should be taxed at 35% or more, at least as high as before 2018.

Corporate profits should be taxed at 21%, as they are today.
Corporate profits should be taxed at about 15%, lower than today.
wealth_tax: Households worth over $50 million should pay 3% or more of their wealth above that amount in tax every year.
Households worth over $50 million should pay about 1% to 2% of their wealth above that amount in tax every year.
There shouldn't be a yearly wealth tax, but big gains in value should be taxed when wealth is passed on at death.
Wealth itself shouldn't be taxed; only income should be.
large_fortunes: Fortunes of $1 billion or more are a problem in themselves, and taxes should be set to shrink them over time.
Billionaires should pay much more in taxes than they do now.
Billionaires should pay somewhat more in taxes than they do now.
Billionaires pay about the right amount in taxes now.
Taxes on billionaires are already too high and hold back investment.
estate_tax_level: Estates worth more than about $1 million should be taxed at death, with rates of 50% or more on the largest.
Estates worth more than about $3.5 million should be taxed at death, at about 45%.
Keep today's estate tax: 40% on the part of an estate above $15 million.
Raise the $15 million threshold so even fewer estates owe the tax.
There should be no tax on estates at death.
inheritance_principle: A large share of inheritances of several million dollars should go to the public, so wealth doesn't pile up across generations.
A moderate tax on inheritances of several million dollars or more is fair.
Only the very largest inheritances should be taxed, and only a little.
Inheritances shouldn't be taxed at all, because the money was already taxed when it was earned.
capital_gains_rate: Profits from selling investments should be taxed at the same rates as wages, for everyone.
High earners should pay wage rates on investment profits; everyone else should keep lower rates.
Investment profits should keep being taxed at lower rates than wages, as they are now.
Investment profits should be taxed at even lower rates than today.
Profits from selling investments shouldn't be taxed at all.
gains_at_death: Gains on investments should be taxed when the owner dies, for gains above about $1 million.
Gains shouldn't be taxed at death, but heirs should owe tax on the whole gain, including the part before they inherited, when they sell.
Keep today's rule: heirs owe tax only on gains made after they inherit, so earlier gains are never taxed.
cash_aid_level: The government should guarantee every household enough to stay above the poverty line.

Cash and food aid should stay at about today's level.

The federal government should end most cash and food aid and leave it to states, charities and families.
aid_form: Aid should come mostly as cash, and people decide for themselves how to spend it.

s: Reducing the gap between rich and poor matters most to me, even if it means higher taxes and slower growth.
I lean toward reducing the gap between rich and poor, even at some cost to growth.
I lean toward focusing on growth, even if the gap between rich and poor widens.
Growth matters most to me; government shouldn't try to shrink the gap between rich and poor, even if it gets wider.
inequality_tradeoff.torn: I weigh reducing the gap and focusing on growth about equally.

deficit_approach: Borrowing is fine for now; the deficit shouldn't be a priority over the next ten years.
The deficit should be closed mainly by raising taxes on high earners and corporations.
The deficit should be closed with about equal parts tax increases and spending cuts.
The deficit should be closed mainly by cutting spending, with some tax increases.
The deficit should be closed entirely by cutting spending, with no tax increases.
balanced_budget_amendment: The Constitution shouldn't require a balanced budget; the government needs to be able to borrow.
The Constitution should require a balanced budget in normal years, with exceptions for wars and recessions.
The Constitution should require a balanced budget every year, with no exceptions, even in a war or recession.
poverty_cause: Most working-age adults who are poor are poor mainly because the economic system is unfair to them.
Most working-age adults who are poor are poor mainly because of circumstances they didn't choose, like where they grew up or bad luck.
Poverty usually comes from a mix of people's circumstances and their own choices.
Most working-age adults who are poor are poor mainly because of their own choices, like dropping out of school or not working.
Most working-age adults who are poor are poor mainly because they don't try hard enough.
job_guarantee: The government should offer a public job, paying at least the minimum wage, to anyone who wants one.
The government should guarantee jobs only in areas with high unemployment.
The government shouldn't guarantee jobs, but it should help with job searches and training.
The government shouldn't provide jobs; jobs should come from private employers.
tips_overtime_tax: Tips and overtime pay should be taxed like any other wages.
Tips and overtime should be free of federal income tax for low- and middle-income workers only.
Tips and overtime should be free of federal income tax for everyone.
